subject: Merchantly POC — Onboarding action plan, success criteria & SDK routing
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Liam Burke <liam.burke@merchantly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Merchantly POC — Onboarding action plan, success criteria & SDK routing

Thanks again for a productive demo this morning, Liam — felt like a great fit for the two use cases you described (fraud signal enrichment for checkout and real-time product suggestions in the cart). Per our call, I wanted to capture next steps and who owns what so we can hit the 3-week POC timeline we discussed.

High-level success criteria (we agreed on):
- Fraud enrichment: end-to-end latency (request -> first token) consistently < 200ms at sample qps=20 (90th pct).
- Quality bar: Precision at top-3 suggestions >= 78% on your seed eval set (see column C of the attached matrix).
- Integration: sample checkout flow instrumented with streaming answers and function/tool-calls to your products API for product detail lookups.

POC milestones & owners (proposed):
1) Week 0 (this week) — Kickoff + environment access — Merchantly: provide sandbox API keys, sample logs, and an eval set (Liam/Priya). Redwood: provision dedicated trial env and share API endpoints (Hannah/Ben).
2) Week 1 — SDK + route wiring: Redwood to provide SDK snippets for streaming + function-call examples and recommended routes for low-latency (Ben). Merchantly to run quick smoke test and share telemetry (Liam).
3) Week 2 — Latency tuning & batching: adjust batching/kv cache policies, run load at target qps, and iterate (Olga + Merchantly infra).
4) Week 3 — Acceptance run & handoff: run acceptance jobs against your eval set, shared dashboard, and signoff (Marissa + Merchantly product/ops).

Immediate asks for your team (Liam/Priya):
- Sandbox API key and a representative subset of purchase logs (anonymized) by EOD Thursday.
- Seed eval set (CSV) with desired labels and a short doc describing the scoring rules.

Attachments: merchantly-poc-matrix.xlsx (POC success metrics, sample eval columns), redwood-integration-proposal-v2.pdf (integration approach).

If that captures things, I’ll schedule the kickoff for Thursday 10/1 at 10am PT — please confirm availability.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

From: Liam Burke <liam.burke@merchantly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya.sinha@merchantly.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merchantly POC — Onboarding action plan, success criteria & SDK routing

Thanks, Hannah — that readout is perfect and aligns with what we agreed. Quick clarifications from our side so we have a clean handoff to engineering: 

- For latency, the 200ms target is measured from Merchantly gateway -> Redwood first token. We will add the network hop to our measurements and supply a short script to reproduce the trace.
- The seed eval set: I’ll send a 500-row CSV with labels and a scoring doc by Thursday morning.
- Regarding tool-calls: the product detail API requires an HMAC-signed header; I’ll include a sandbox key and the signing example in the artifacts.

We’re available for the Thursday 10/1 10am PT kickoff. Priya and I will loop in Engineering and a point from Legal for the NDA/Docs (they may want to see the proposal PDF).

One ask on timing: can Redwood share the SDK snippets (specifically streaming + function-calls) before the kickoff? That will let our engs scan the pattern and avoid firewall surprises during Week 1.

— Liam
Liam Burke
Head of Product, Merchantly
liam.burke@merchantly.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Merchantly POC — Onboarding action plan, success criteria & SDK routing (internal)

Internal ops note / proposed task split based on Hannah’s plan and Liam’s asks: 

- Ben: Own SDK + route examples. Deliverables: streaming example (Node + Python), function-calling example that demonstrates HMAC-signed tool-calls, and a small sample app (zip) that Merchantly can run locally. ETA: share snippets by Thu 10/1 06:00 PT. Attachment: sample-sdk-snippets.zip (contains README and quickstart).
- Olga: Infra tuning + acceptance harness. I’ll hand off target load profile and the 90th pct latency dashboard to you; please outline the batching and kv-cache defaults we should start with for their QPS=20 workload. Target: initial tuning by Wed 10/7.
- Marissa: Instrumentation & eval dashboard. Create a shared Grafana view and set up the eval-job pipeline to compute top-3 precision automatically. ETA: 10/8 for dashboard skeleton.

Notes on the SDK snippets (quick bullets to include in the public snippets):
- Use streaming responses for product suggestions to ensure the UI gets partial suggestions quickly. Include guidance to set max_tokens low for the first-stream chunk.
- Show how to attach an HMAC header to function/tool calls and an idempotency key for the product detail lookup.
- Recommend a prefix/KV cache for known user context (cart items) to reduce token cost on repeated lookups.

I’ll reply-all with the zip and a link to an internal runbook once I upload artifacts to the shared Drive. 

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Hi all — confirming receipt of the attachments and our availability for the 10/1 kickoff at 10am PT. A few items from Legal/Product that we’ll need addressed during the kickoff: 

- Minimal data handling note: we need confirmation Redwood will not persist raw customer PII and that logs in the trial environment can be redacted. Please have a short statement ready (even a one-paragraph note is fine).
- Timeline: Legal would like the acceptance window to include 2 business days for us to review the acceptance run results before signing off. Please note that in the acceptance checklist.
- Docs: I’ve uploaded an internal summary to our Drive and shared access (link below). We’ll attach the sandbox keys and the HMAC signing example there.

Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Merchantly-poc-artifacts

Thanks, looking forward to the kickoff.

— Priya
